```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Bins_2019_pazopanib"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-018-0719-5> (open access)

Bins et al. genotyped 94 of the 96 patients behind the Yu 2017 pazopanib
population PK model and re-fitted that model with four candidate
polymorphisms in the pazopanib elimination pathway. Only *CYP3A4\*22*
(rs35599367) was retained: carriers have a 36% lower clearance (0.18 vs
0.28 L/h). The packaged file is the final model of the paper's Electronic
Supplementary Material (the NONMEM control stream) with the final estimates of
Table 4.

The structure is the Yu 2017 model:

* Each dose is split over two parallel first-order absorption routes. 36% of
  the bioavailable dose is absorbed by a fast route (KaF 0.39 1/h, no lag) and
  64% by a slow route (KaS 0.12 1/h) that starts after a 0.97 h lag.
* Two-compartment disposition with linear clearance.
* Relative bioavailability falls with the dose (1 at 200 mg, an Emax decrease
  above it with ED50 466 mg) and decays over the treatment course to 49% of
  its starting value (rate 0.16 per day).
* Pazopanib clearance is multiplied by the relative amount of a metabolic
  enzyme pool that co-administered ifosfamide induces. The ifosfamide model is
  the Kerbusch 2000 autoinduction model, fixed (`Kerbusch_2000_ifosfamide` in
  this library). Without ifosfamide the enzyme pool stays at 1.

# Population

The 94 patients came from three Dutch studies: a pazopanib therapeutic drug
monitoring study (13 patients), a phase I pazopanib + docetaxel study (40) and
a phase I pazopanib + ifosfamide study (41); 761 plasma samples (Bins 2019
Table 2). 71% were male and 97% Caucasian; median age 57 years (IQR 48-64).
Starting doses ranged from 200 to 1000 mg once daily. Tumour types varied and
were not recorded. Eleven patients were heterozygous *CYP3A4\*1/\*22* and none
homozygous (Table 1).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Bins_2019_pazopanib")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lka_fast` (KaF) | 0.39 1/h | Table 4 final model; control stream THETA(3) |
| `lka_slow` (KaS) | 0.12 1/h | Table 4; THETA(4) |
| `logitfrel` (fast fraction) | logit(0.36) | Table 4 'Fraction of fast absorption' 36%; THETA(10) is the odds, `F1 = TVFR / (1 + TVFR) * TVF` |
| `ltlag` (slow-route lag) | 0.97 h | Table 4; THETA(5) `ALAG3` |
| `lcl` | 0.28 L/h | Table 4; THETA(1) |
| `e_snp_cyp3a4_rs35599367_cl` | 0.18 / 0.28 = 0.643 | Table 4 'Clearance CYP3A4\*22' 0.18 L/h; Methods `Ppop = theta_x * theta_y^pg`; THETA(13) |
| `lvc` | 2.4 L | Table 4; THETA(2) |
| `lq` | 0.97 L/h | Table 4; THETA(6) |
| `lvp` | 24.3 L | Table 4; THETA(7) |
| `lfdepot` (rF at 200 mg) | 1 FIX | Yu 2017 Table 2; control stream `TVB = 1` at `DOSE = 200` |
| `lemax` (Emax of the dose effect) | 1 FIX | Yu 2017 Table 2; THETA(9) `VMAXDOSE` (1 FIX) |
| `led50` | 466 mg | Table 4 'Dose level with half of bioavailability at dose 200 mg'; THETA(8) |
| `lfdepot_exp_inf` | 1 - 0.51 = 0.49 | Table 4 'Magnitude of decrease in relative bioavailability in time' 51%; THETA(12) `DCRP` |
| `lfdepot_exp_kdes` | 0.16 / 24 1/h | Table 4 'First-order decay constant' 0.16 per day; `LAMBDA = THETA(11) / 24` |
| IIV KaF, CL, Vp, rF | 142%, 27%, 98%, 38% CV | Table 4 'Between-subject variability' |
| IOV rF | 76% CV | Table 4 'Within-subject variability'; `$OMEGA BLOCK(1)` x 3 by `PKDAY` |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 8.0%, 2.91 mg/L | Table 4 'Residual unexplained variability'; `Y = IPRED * (1 + ERR(1)) + ERR(2)` |
| Ifosfamide CL, V, K_enz,out, IC50 and IIV | 2.94 L/h, 43.5 L, 0.0546 1/h, 30.7 uM; 24.5%, 23.4%, 22.7% | Kerbusch 2000 Table 1 (fixed); control stream data items `ICLI`, `IVI`, `IKENZ`, `IIC50` |
| Dose-dependent rF | `1 - Emax * (DOSE - 200) / (ED50 + DOSE - 200)` | control stream `TVB`; Yu 2017 Eq. 3 |
| Time-dependent rF | `1 - Ad + Ad * exp(-k * TIME)` | control stream `TVF1`; Yu 2017 Eq. 4 |
| Combined rF | `TVB * TVF1 * exp(eta_F + eta_IOV)` | control stream `TVF`; Yu 2017 Eq. 5 |
| Pazopanib elimination | `K20 * A(5) * A(2)` | control stream `$DES` |
| Enzyme pool | `KENZ - KENZ * A(5) * (1 - CPI / (CPI + IC50I))`, `A_0(5) = 1` | control stream `$DES`; Kerbusch 2000 Eq. 4 |

# Simulation helpers

The dose-dependent bioavailability reads `DOSE_PAZOPANIB_MG` and the
time-dependent bioavailability reads `T_FIRSTDOSE` on every dose record, so the
event tables list each dose explicitly instead of using `addl` (an
`addl`-expanded dose would carry the covariates of its parent record and freeze
`T_FIRSTDOSE` at 0). Each dose goes to both `depot` and `depot2`.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Bins_2019_pazopanib")

make_pazopanib_events <- function(ids, dose, n_days, tau = 24, obs_times = numeric(0), snp = 0) {
  dose_times <- seq(0, n_days * 24 - tau, by = tau)
  one <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_times, amt = dose, cmt = "depot", evid = 1L),
    data.frame(time = dose_times, amt = dose, cmt = "depot2", evid = 1L),
    data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, cmt = "central", evid = 0L)
  )
  bind_rows(lapply(ids, function(i) mutate(one, id = i))) |>
    mutate(
      DOSE_PAZOPANIB_MG = dose,
      SNP_CYP3A4_RS35599367 = snp,
      T_FIRSTDOSE = time,
      OCC = 1L
    ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
```

# Bioavailability against Yu 2017

Yu 2017 reports two closed-form consequences of the bioavailability model: at
800 mg once daily the relative bioavailability falls from 44% at the start of
treatment to 22% after 8 weeks, and the relative bioavailability of a 400 mg
dose is 59% higher than that of an 800 mg dose. Both follow from the packaged
parameters (Yu 2017 used ED50 480 mg; Bins 2019 re-estimated 466 mg).

```{r bioavailability}
rf <- function(dose, t_h) {
  (1 - (dose - 200) / (466 + dose - 200)) * (0.49 + 0.51 * exp(-0.16 / 24 * t_h))
}
rf_tab <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("rF, 800 mg, first dose", "rF, 800 mg, week 8", "rF(400 mg) / rF(800 mg)"),
  Packaged = c(rf(800, 0), rf(800, 8 * 7 * 24), rf(400, 0) / rf(800, 0)),
  "Yu 2017" = c(0.44, 0.22, 1.59),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(rf_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Relative bioavailability (Yu 2017 Results and Discussion).")
stopifnot(all(abs(rf_tab$Packaged / rf_tab$`Yu 2017` - 1) < 0.05))
```

# Steady-state troughs by genotype (ESM Table 1, Figure 2)

The paper simulated 500 patients per genotype and dose (400, 600 and 800 mg
once daily) and reported the trough 6 weeks after the start of treatment
(Electronic Supplementary Material Table 1). The median trough of a log-normal
cohort is the typical-value trough, so the deterministic solve with all random
effects zeroed must reproduce the published medians.

```{r typical-troughs}
esm <- data.frame(
  genotype = rep(c("Wild type", "*22 carrier"), each = 3),
  SNP = rep(0:1, each = 3),
  dose = rep(c(400, 600, 800), 2),
  med = c(15.9, 18.4, 19.7, 26.5, 30.6, 34.6),
  lower = c(7.2, 8.3, 8.5, 11.7, 13.5, 15.5),
  upper = c(36.6, 42.2, 45.9, 60.7, 70.0, 77.6),
  pct_above = c(33, 42, 46, 74, 81, 83)
)
trough_time <- 42 * 24

typ_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(esm)), function(i) {
  make_pazopanib_events(i, esm$dose[i], n_days = 42, obs_times = trough_time, snp = esm$SNP[i])
}))
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events) |> as.data.frame()

esm$typical <- typ$Cc[typ$time == trough_time]
esm$pct_diff <- 100 * (esm$typical / esm$med - 1)
esm |>
  transmute(
    Genotype = genotype, "Dose (mg QD)" = dose,
    "Published median (mg/L)" = med,
    "Typical value (mg/L)" = round(typical, 1),
    "Difference (%)" = round(pct_diff, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Week-6 trough: typical value versus ESM Table 1 median.")
# Deterministic on our side; the published median carries Monte Carlo error
# from 500 subjects (about 3-4%). A wrong CL, ED50, decay or CYP3A4*22 factor
# moves these by 10% or more.
stopifnot(all(abs(esm$pct_diff) < 6))
```

The typical-value steady-state profiles over the week-6 dosing interval
reproduce Figure 2 of the paper:

```{r figure2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
fig2_arms <- expand.grid(SNP = 0:1, dose = c(600, 800))
fig2_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(fig2_arms)), function(i) {
  make_pazopanib_events(
    i, fig2_arms$dose[i], n_days = 43,
    obs_times = seq(41 * 24, 42 * 24, by = 0.25), snp = fig2_arms$SNP[i]
  )
}))
fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = fig2_events) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  left_join(mutate(fig2_arms, id = row_number()), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    Genotype = ifelse(SNP == 1, "CYP3A4*22", "Wild type"),
    Regimen = paste(dose, "mg QD")
  )
ggplot(fig2, aes(time - 41 * 24, Cc, colour = Genotype, linetype = Regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 20.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("CYP3A4*22" = "red", "Wild type" = "black")) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose at week 6 (h)", y = "Pazopanib (mg/L)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Bins 2019 (dotted line: 20.5 mg/L target trough).")
```

## Simulated cohorts

The spread in ESM Table 1 is reproduced when the simulation omits the
inter-occasion variability on bioavailability (one occasion per subject would
add it once; the published bounds are too narrow for that). The published
columns labelled "interquartile range" match the 5th and 95th percentiles of
such a cohort, and the percentage of subjects above the 20.5 mg/L target is
consistent with the same spread. The cohort below uses 200 subjects per arm
without IOV: the model applies the IOV etas only on records with `OCC` 1-3,
so `OCC = 0` switches it off.

```{r cohort}
n_per_arm <- 200
cohort_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(esm)), function(i) {
  make_pazopanib_events(
    (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm), esm$dose[i],
    n_days = 42, obs_times = trough_time, snp = esm$SNP[i]
  ) |> mutate(arm = i, OCC = 0L)
}))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190401)
cohort <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = cohort_events, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame()

cohort_tab <- cohort |>
  filter(time == trough_time) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    sim_med = median(sim), sim_p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), sim_p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    sim_pct = 100 * mean(sim > 20.5), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  bind_cols(esm)
cohort_tab |>
  transmute(
    Genotype = genotype, "Dose (mg QD)" = dose,
    "Median sim / pub" = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", sim_med, med),
    "5th pct sim / pub 'lower'" = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", sim_p05, lower),
    "95th pct sim / pub 'upper'" = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", sim_p95, upper),
    "% > 20.5 mg/L sim / pub" = sprintf("%.0f / %.0f", sim_pct, pct_above)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Week-6 trough distribution, 200 subjects per arm (no IOV), versus ESM Table 1.")
# Centre: within 15% of the published median (MC error of 200 subjects is
# about 6%). Spread: the share above target within 15 points (binomial SE
# about 3.5 points), which would fail if the full IOV were included
# (wild type 400 mg rises to about 42%, carriers at 800 mg fall to about 72%).
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cohort_tab$sim_med / cohort_tab$med - 1)) < 0.15,
  all(abs(cohort_tab$sim_pct - cohort_tab$pct_above) < 15)
)
```

# PKNCA: week-6 dosing interval against Yu 2017

Yu 2017 simulated 800 mg once daily against 400 mg twice daily for 6 weeks and
reported the week-6 24-hour AUC (665 vs 1056 mg*h/L) and trough (22 vs
39 mg/L). Those numbers come from the Yu 2017 base model (CL 0.27 L/h, ED50
480 mg, decay 0.15 per day); the Bins 2019 final model re-estimated these to
0.28 L/h, 466 mg and 0.16 per day, which lowers the 24-hour AUC by about 7%.
The comparison below runs PKNCA on the typical-value week-6 profiles of wild
type patients.

```{r pknca}
nca_arms <- data.frame(treatment = c("800 mg QD", "400 mg BID"), dose = c(800, 400), tau = c(24, 12))
t0 <- 41 * 24
nca_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(nca_arms)), function(i) {
  make_pazopanib_events(
    i, nca_arms$dose[i], n_days = 42, tau = nca_arms$tau[i],
    obs_times = seq(t0, t0 + 24, by = 0.25)
  ) |> mutate(treatment = nca_arms$treatment[i])
}))
nca_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = nca_events, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

# Re-base the week-6 day to start at 0 so the interval starts at 0.
conc_df <- nca_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= t0, time <= t0 + 24) |>
  mutate(time = time - t0) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- nca_events |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot", time >= t0, time < t0 + 24) |>
  transmute(id, time = time - t0, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("800 mg QD", "400 mg BID"),
  auclast = c(665, 1056),
  cmin = c(22, 39)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res, reference,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmin = "mg/L", cmax = "mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Typical-value week-6 NCA (0-24 h) versus Yu 2017 Results 3.3.")

sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  left_join(reference, by = "treatment")
# Different (base vs final) parameter sets on the two sides: a 15% band
# covers the 7% parameter shift; a wrong dose split or F model is off by 40%+.
stopifnot(all(abs(sim_auc$PPORRES / sim_auc$auclast - 1) < 0.15))
```

# Ifosfamide induction

The model carries the ifosfamide-driven enzyme pool so that pazopanib can be
simulated alongside an ifosfamide infusion. The example below gives 800 mg
pazopanib once daily for 3 weeks and, from day 14, a 72-hour infusion of
9 g/m^2 ifosfamide at a body-surface area of 1.8 m^2. This is the Kerbusch 2000
regimen; the paper does not print the ifosfamide schedule of its study 3.
Ifosfamide doses are in umol (molar mass 261.09 g/mol), the unit of the
Kerbusch 2000 model.

```{r ifosfamide, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ifo_umol <- 9 * 1.8 * 1e6 / 261.09
ifo_start <- 13 * 24
paz <- make_pazopanib_events(1, 800, n_days = 21, obs_times = seq(0, 21 * 24, by = 1))
ifo <- data.frame(
  id = 1, time = ifo_start, amt = ifo_umol, rate = ifo_umol / 72,
  cmt = "central_ifosfamide", evid = 1L,
  DOSE_PAZOPANIB_MG = 800, SNP_CYP3A4_RS35599367 = 0, OCC = 1L
) |> mutate(T_FIRSTDOSE = time)
both <- bind_rows(paz, ifo) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
alone <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = paz) |> as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(scenario = "pazopanib alone")
combo <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = both) |> as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(scenario = "with ifosfamide on days 14-16")

ggplot(bind_rows(alone, combo), aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Pazopanib (mg/L)", colour = NULL)

# Kerbusch 2000 Results: 'during the first 24 h ... the model predicted an
# average doubling of the relative enzyme amount'.
enz_24 <- combo$enz_pool[combo$time == ifo_start + 24]
enz_24
stopifnot(
  all(abs(alone$enz_pool - 1) < 1e-8),
  enz_24 > 1.6, enz_24 < 2.6,
  combo$Cc[combo$time == ifo_start + 72] < alone$Cc[alone$time == ifo_start + 72]
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **CYP3A4\*22 clearance.** Table 4 prints the carrier clearance (0.18 L/h)
  rather than the multiplier THETA(13); the multiplier is 0.18 / 0.28 = 0.643.
  Table 3 and the Results text quote the wild-type clearance as 0.27 L/h
  (giving the abstract's "35% lower"); the final-model column of Table 4
  (0.28 L/h) is used, and with it the typical-value troughs reproduce ESM
  Table 1 within 3.5%.
* **Fraction absorbed by the fast route.** The control stream estimates the
  odds `TVFR` with its eta fixed to 0; Table 4 prints the fraction (36%). It is
  encoded as `logitfrel = logit(0.36)`, which is the same model.
* **Time-dependent bioavailability.** Table 4 prints the magnitude of the
  decrease Ad (51%); it is encoded through the registered asymptote parameter
  `fdepot_exp_inf = 1 - Ad`. The decay constant is printed per day and divided
  by 24 in the control stream, so `T_FIRSTDOSE` is in hours since the first
  pazopanib dose (the control stream uses the NONMEM `TIME` item).
* **Variance scale.** Table 4 reports between- and within-subject variability
  as CV%. The variances use `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. Neither the paper nor
  Yu 2017 states the conversion; the ESM Table 1 trough distribution cannot
  separate it from `omega^2 = CV^2`, because the two readings differ materially
  only for the fast absorption rate (142%) and the peripheral volume (98%),
  which barely move a 24-hour trough.
* **Simulation spread in ESM Table 1.** The published trough bounds and the
  percentage above target are reproduced only when the inter-occasion
  variability is omitted, and the columns labelled "interquartile range"
  match the 5th and 95th percentiles. The packaged model keeps the IOV (it is
  part of the fitted model); the vignette removes it only to reproduce the
  published simulation. The table also labels concentrations in ug/L; they are
  mg/L, the unit of the model and of the 20.5 mg/L target.
* **Inter-occasion variability.** One eta per sampling occasion (`OCC` 1-3,
  the control stream's `PKDAY`), each with the same variance. Records with
  `OCC` outside 1-3 get no IOV; NONMEM would instead carry over the last
  assigned value.
* **Ifosfamide sub-model.** The source data supplied each patient's individual
  ifosfamide parameters (empirical Bayes estimates from the Kerbusch 2000
  model). The packaged model replaces them with the Kerbusch 2000 typical
  values and between-subject variability, fixed. Ifosfamide doses and
  concentrations are in umol and umol/L, the Kerbusch 2000 units. The
  ifosfamide residual error is not carried because ifosfamide concentrations
  were not an output of this model.
* **IPRED floor.** The control stream floors the prediction at 0.001 mg/L
  before applying the residual error; the packaged model does not.
* **Docetaxel.** Docetaxel co-administration had no effect on pazopanib PK
  (Yu 2017) and is not part of the model.
